newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil probes Mafia money laundering in bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Brazil probes Mafia money laundering in bolsa.

text.p: Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) is investigating possible money laundering operations by the Italian Mafia on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange, a CVM spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

The CVM decided to carry out an inquiry following last week's arrest of Italian Domenico Verde, 56, in the northeastern city of Maceio, Alagoas state. He was arrested in response to an extradition request by Italian authorities, who accuse him of involvement with the Mafia.
"We are investigating whether Verde used the Rio stock exchange for money laundering operations," the spokeswoman said.

The non-governmental organisation Instituto Brasileiro Giovanni Falcone (IBGF) says Brazil is the favourite hideout in South America for Italian criminals on the run from authorities at home, O Globo newspaper said. The IBGF says around 50 Italian criminals are currently living in Brazil.

Meanwhile, Brazilian Federal Police are investigating the possibility that Verde was involved in money laundering operations with Paulo Cesar Farias, the murdered aide of disgraced former President Fernando Collor.
Verde, who has been living in Brazil since 1993 and has become a naturalised Brazilian, denies being in the Mafia and says he does not know Farias.

Brazilian police were given evidence by their Italian colleagues in March of bank transfers worth $7.8 million between Farias and Italian drug traffickers. The transactions were uncovered by Italian police tracing the origin of deposits in Mafia accounts.
The finds came four years after police began investigating an alleged infuence-peddling scheme, believed to have been masterminded by Farias, that forced Collor to resign in 1992.

Farias and his girlfriend Suzana Marcolino were found shot to death in June 1996 at Farias' beach house in Maceio. Brazilian authorities recently decided to re-open the probe into the murder after a new forensic report contradicted the earlier official version that Farias was shot by Marcolino, who then committed suicide.
